terms.definition: The dense, positively charged core at the center of an atom.
terms.function: Holds the protons and neutrons and nearly all the atom's mass.
terms.whereItIs: The small bundle of spheres at the center of the model.
terms.whyItMatters: The nucleus holds the atom's identity, mass, and nuclear energy.

terms.definition: A positively charged particle packed in the nucleus.
terms.function: Gives the nucleus its positive charge and defines the element.
terms.whereItIs: The red spheres in the nucleus bundle.
terms.whyItMatters: The proton count is the element's identity number.

terms.definition: A charge-free particle packed in the nucleus.
terms.function: Adds mass and stability to the nucleus.
terms.whereItIs: The gray spheres in the nucleus bundle.
terms.whyItMatters: Neutron counts create isotopes of the same element.

terms.definition: The total mass of the atom, almost entirely from its nucleus.
terms.function: Measures an atom's weight, dominated by protons and neutrons.
terms.whereItIs: Reflected by the heavy nucleus bundle in the model.
terms.whyItMatters: Explains why the atom's mass sits in its tiny core.
